AI for GP Practices and Allied Health -- Reducing Admin, Protecting Care Time

By Craig Wilson  ·  Category: Industry Use Cases  ·  Read time: 7 min  ·  Keyword: AI for GP practices Australia

Australian GPs and allied health practitioners are spending 40–50% of their clinical time on administrative tasks. Here's what AI can address -- and the compliance boundaries that matter.

AI for Australian GP practices and allied health is addressing four administrative burdens: clinical documentation (3–5 minutes recovered per consultation), referral letter generation (10–15 minutes per referral reduced to 2–3 minutes of review), results management, and patient recall. Every system is designed with strict compliance requirements: patient consent for any consultation recording, practitioner review and authorisation of all AI-assisted documentation, data processing within Australian infrastructure only.

A 2024 RACGP survey found that GPs spend an average of 40% of their working time on administrative tasks rather than direct patient care. For allied health practitioners -- physiotherapists, occupational therapists, psychologists, speech pathologists -- the ratio is similar. AI addresses the administrative layer surrounding clinical work without touching the clinical judgment.

What AI can address in Australian general practice and allied health

Clinical documentation assistance

An AI clinical documentation system uses the consultation recording (with patient consent) or the practitioner's dictation to produce a structured draft note. The practitioner reviews, edits, and finalises. The documentation process that currently takes 5–8 minutes per consultation can be reduced to 1–2 minutes of review time.

Compliance requirement: Patients must provide explicit informed consent for any consultation recording. The practitioner reviews and approves every note and remains the author of record.

Realistic outcome: 3–5 minutes recovered per consultation. For a GP with 25 daily consultations, that's 75–125 minutes per day -- potentially 4–6 additional patient appointments in recovered time.

Referral letter generation

An AI referral system drafts referral letters from the consultation notes and patient record, pre-populated with the relevant clinical information. The practitioner reviews for clinical accuracy and adds any specific communication to the specialist.

Realistic outcome: 10–15 minutes per referral reduced to 2–3 minutes of review. For practices with high referral volumes, this is significant.

Results management and patient recall

An AI results management system flags results requiring urgent attention, categorises by action required, and can draft routine patient communications for practitioner review.

An AI recall management system monitors patient records against defined recall criteria and generates a daily list of patients due for follow-up -- ensuring no patient who should be recalled is missed.

The compliance framework for healthcare AI in Australia

Healthcare AI in Australia operates within the Privacy Act 1988, the My Health Records Act, state and territory health records legislation, and professional registration standards. Critical requirements:

  • Patient data processed within Australian infrastructure only
  • Human review and authorisation of all clinical outputs before entering the record
  • Complete audit trails of AI-assisted documentation

What AI implementation costs for a healthcare practice

Discovery Sprint ($5,000–$12,000): A compliance-first assessment of your current systems, documentation burden, and the highest-ROI starting point. Includes review of Privacy Act and professional registration requirements for your specific context.

Phase 2 Build -- Documentation Assistance ($25,000–$55,000): Integration with your clinical software (Best Practice, Medical Director, Nookal, Cliniko), documentation assistance system, and practitioner review workflow. Typically 5–7 weeks.

Frequently asked questions

Is AI clinical documentation compliant with Australian healthcare law?

Yes, when designed correctly. The systems we build process data within Australian infrastructure, require explicit patient consent for any recording, and require practitioner review and authorisation before any AI-assisted documentation enters the patient record. The practitioner is the clinical author of record.

How much does AI for a GP practice cost in Australia?

A Discovery Sprint costs $5,000–$12,000. Documentation assistance for a practice with 3–5 practitioners typically costs $25,000–$55,000 to build and integrate. Most practices see payback within 6–9 months through recovered consultation time.

Does the AI work with Best Practice or Medical Director?

Yes -- we build integrations with the major Australian clinical software platforms. The specific integration pathway depends on your platform version, which the Discovery Sprint assesses.

What happens to patient data -- does it leave Australia?

No. All patient data is processed within Australian infrastructure. We don't use offshore AI processing for any clinical data. This is a hard requirement in our system design for healthcare clients.
